input.quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise; provided that the acquiring party agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 18.9 is mutual and already delivers most of the fallback: either Party may assign to an acquirer of substantially all of its business or assets without consent (successor right), that acquirer must deliver a written assumption to the non-assigning Party (written notice), and all other assignments — including to an Affiliate — require the other Party's written consent. The one material gap is that the general consent gate for non-successor assignments is unqualified, so Array could withhold consent arbitrarily; the fallback requires that consent not be unreasonably withheld. We therefore inserted the reasonableness standard into the first sentence only, leaving the successor carve-out and Affiliate mechanic untouched. Change of control is not a concern: Section 18.10 (and the Section 4.5(b) reference at p0322) address only a Change in Control of Array and give Array no termination or re-pricing right on Ono's change of control. We note the Affiliate consent proviso permits refusal where the non-assigning Party reasonably believes material adverse tax consequences would result; that is a reasonableness-based, mutual qualification and we have not disturbed it.

ops.oldText: This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto;
ops.newText: This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed;

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added the customary reasonableness standard to the consent gate in Section 18.9, so neither Party can arbitrarily block a non-successor assignment. The mutual successor carve-out and the Affiliate assignment mechanic are unchanged.
proposal.summary: Consent to non-successor assignments not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
